questions.question: When you use alcohol and drugs together, the effects are:

options.text: Less dangerous than using either one alone.
Stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes them even more dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Move to another lane and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to move to another lane and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous because they may continue tailgating at your new, faster speed.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just a normal part of riding.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wearing ear protection while riding protects your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These services include rest areas, gas stations, restaurants, and hospitals.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves when riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Make larger zigzag motions to signal other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to zigzag to stay in your lane is more dangerous than just riding straight.

questions.question: The best way to avoid getting tired on a long motorcycle trip is to:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, limit your riding time each day and take frequent breaks to rest. Do not use stimulant drugs because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: All keep safe distances between each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All keep safe distances between each other.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay together while keeping safe distances from each other.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have better control of their motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast causes you to lose control. Your motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing when buying a motorcycle helmet. Choose a helmet that fastens securely, fits well, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is over.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After hitting an object on the road, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt before you ride again.

questions.question: When traveling at night, it is:

options.text: Easier to judge distances than during the day.
Just as easy to judge distances as during the day.
Harder to judge distances than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to judge distances than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances when driving at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see how far away things are. At night, artificial lights may distort these visual clues or make them disappear completely.

questions.question: When being followed too closely by another vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to continue tailgating you, just at a higher speed.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, it is better to ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: No matter what helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives the best protection when it meets DOT and state safety standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Be loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Fit snug enough to stop flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to limit movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough to stop flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: There is less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning, such as when turning, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do it very carefully.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced:
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding, no matter how slowly you go. Wearing a quality helmet properly reduces this risk greatly.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible, signal your turns, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: What can a motorcycle rider carry?

options.text: A small package in one hand.
A package with their hands if it does not block their view.

questions.explanation: In Alabama, you cannot carry anything while riding a motorcycle. You must keep both hands on the handlebars at all times.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Refuse to move to avoid hazards.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road. This gives you time to react to problems before you reach them.

questions.question: What color should you wear to be more visible during the day?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like yellow, orange, red, or green. Most crashes happen in daylight, so bright clothing helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in a lane?

options.text: Where other drivers can see you and you have space around your bike.
Anywhere you want without thinking about others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where other drivers can see you and you have space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have safe space around your motorcycle. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: Do motorcycles have blind spots?

options.text: No, other drivers can always see them.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: What material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and strong synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Why should you wear bright clothes during the day?

options.text: You do not need to wear bright clothes during the day.
Most crashes happen in daylight, so bright clothes help you be seen.
You should wear dark clothes during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most crashes happen in daylight, so bright clothes help you be seen.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with lights flashing?

options.text: Stop behind the emergency vehicle on the road.
Stop and wait for it to move.
Move to another lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from it.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.
